clue.text: May committee use it as a launching-pad?

parts.note: May is a month of the spring season
a board is a governing committee, as in a board of directors

explanation.surface: A question about whether a committee might use something to launch a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' at the start looks like the verb of permission; here it is the month, standing for its season.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving or gymnastics platform that propels you upward, figuratively a starting point for a career.

clue.text: Wine and dine leading advocate

indicators.note: dine leading wine puts the word for dining in front of the word for wine

parts.note: to sup is to eat an evening meal
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Advice to serve wine and food, with a leading advocate as guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' tells you the dining word goes first, before the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To back or champion a cause is to argue for it, the verb sense of advocate.

clue.text: Marsupials need time to settle down

parts.note: roos is short for kangaroos, which are marsupials

explanation.surface: Kangaroos and their kin need a while to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds perch for the night when they settle down to sleep.

clue.text: Fruit producing delicious drink in the Orient

parts.note: nectar is the drink of the gods, any delicious drink
taken as written
E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: A fruit that yields a delicious drink somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach.

clue.text: Rage resulting from skin infection

explanation.surface: Anger caused by a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe with anger is to rage; a pus-filled inflamed swelling on the skin is the other sense.

clue.text: Bill and associate are fairly competent

parts.note: an ad is a bill or poster advertising something
to equate things is to associate or link them

explanation.surface: Bill and his colleague are reasonably good at the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name; it is a poster, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory or sufficient, good enough without being outstanding.

clue.text: Spartan style of architecture

explanation.surface: A plain, austere look in building design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' looks like the adjective meaning austere; here it means belonging to Sparta, whose people were Dorians.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Dorian Greeks of Sparta; also the plainest of the classical column orders.

clue.text: Traps engineer into getting a tonic

parts.note: gins are snares or traps for game

explanation.surface: Someone snares an engineer to give them a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traps' looks like a verb with 'engineer' its object; it is the noun GINS, snares.
explanation.definitionFit: A root used in herbal medicine as a restorative stimulant.

clue.text: Winning by taking on staff

explanation.surface: Succeeding in business through recruitment.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming or attractive, as a winning smile is; also hiring or employing people.

clue.text: Bar paid copywriter

parts.note: a pro is a professional, someone paid for the work
a scribe copied manuscripts by hand

explanation.surface: A pub's hired advertising writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub; it is the verb meaning forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid or ban something officially.

clue.text: Enter at speed to make arrest

explanation.surface: Police rush in to make an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash inside; also slang for taking someone into custody.

clue.text: Not in place to present expenses

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
to lay is to put or place something down

explanation.surface: Someone away from their seat presenting a claim for expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent on something, total spending or expenditure.

clue.text: A buyer's leverage

explanation.surface: The bargaining power a customer holds.
explanation.definitionFit: What a shopper acquires; also a firm grip giving mechanical advantage.

clue.text: A poison reportedly causing alarm

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for a poison is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: A poison that, by all accounts, is causing panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell rung as a warning signal.

clue.text: Mates without money working at last

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for mates goes around the money

parts.note: cobbers is Australian slang for mates, friends
L stands for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Friends with no cash who finally have jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means lacking on the surface but outside here; 'at last' seems to mean finally, but a last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped form.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoemakers and menders shape boots over a last, a wooden foot model.

clue.text: First-rate currency

explanation.surface: A top-quality currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent or of the highest quality; also British money, the pound.

clue.text: Move round behind old stove

parts.note: rear is the back, behind
a range is an old-fashioned cooking stove

explanation.surface: Shift an old cooker round to the back of the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: To change the order or position of things.

clue.text: Fruit grown by worker in the veld

indicators.note: in tells you the worker goes inside the word for the grassland

parts.note: the veld is South African open grassland, a plain
a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: Fruit grown by a farm labourer on the South African grasslands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' suggests a farmhand; it is an ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy banana-like fruit eaten cooked.

clue.text: Hesitation by British woman to take cover

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: After some dithering, a British woman takes shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy carried for shelter from the rain; also an overall protection.

clue.text: American male gets embarrassed when escorted

parts.note: US means American
he is the male pronoun
red, as when blushing with embarrassment

explanation.surface: An American man blushes as he is led along.
explanation.definitionFit: Guided or shown the way, as theatre staff lead people to seats.

clue.text: Obsession makes Chinese boxer withdraw

parts.note: the Han are the main ethnic group of China

indicators.note: withdraw means draw back, so the word for a boxer is turned round

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A fixation causes a Chinese fighter to pull out of a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter of any sort, but here it is the short word for a pugilist, and 'withdraw' says to read it backwards after the Chinese people.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurotic preoccupation or emotional problem one can't shake off.

clue.text: Mantrap proves a hazard

explanation.surface: A trap set for people turns out dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealed hole for catching people or animals; also a hidden danger.

clue.text: Quite determined the man will get nicked

parts.note: he'll is a contraction of he will
bent is slang for stolen, nicked

explanation.surface: A determined man will end up arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' suggests arrested; here it means stolen, which is BENT in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Recklessly resolved on a course of action.

clue.text: Building society holding bad accounts

indicators.note: holding means the abbreviation for building society contains the word for bad

parts.note: BS is the abbreviation for a building society, a British mutual savings lender
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A lender keeps bad debts on its books.
explanation.definitionFit: Statements of money owed, such as invoices.

clue.text: Lending facility is a source of pride

explanation.surface: Being able to borrow is something to be proud of.
explanation.definitionFit: Money lent on trust; also honour or distinction, as when someone is a credit to their family.

clue.text: Tenor wants to live aimlessly

explanation.surface: A singer who wants an idle life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' looks like a singer; it means the gist or general sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The general meaning of a speech; also to wander through life without purpose.

clue.text: Fruit popular with the Italian

parts.note: U as in a U film certificate, universal and for everyone
gli is the Italian plural definite article

explanation.surface: A fruit that Italians love.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican hybrid citrus, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Foremost Russian mountain range in the country

indicators.note: foremost picks the first letter of the word Russian

parts.note: the Urals are the mountain range dividing Europe from Asia

explanation.surface: Russia's leading mountains lie out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to farmland and villages rather than towns.

clue.text: Agent Iran replaced in s. America

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A spy from Iran is moved to a posting in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation located on the southern continent, an example of a country there.

clue.text: Breakdown entitles man to become emotional

indicators.note: a breakdown splits things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous breakdown gives a man licence to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing tender feelings, mawkish or nostalgic.
